angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 411,159 km at 192.10 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.2055 +/- 0.0235 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 192.10 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.591 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract): 411,159 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.612 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3775 +/- 59 K from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7189.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.682, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
